title: Lombok vs Flores: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Flores for Komodo dragons, dramatic national park, and world-class diving. Lombok for beaches, surf, Rinjani trekking, and easier logistics. Do both via the 4-day sailing trip if you have 10+ days.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Lombok has more white-sand beaches, easier to reach independently. Flores has Pink Beach and Padar Island but requires boat tours.

categories.name: Wildlife
categories.summary: Flores wins with Komodo dragons (a globally unique experience) and manta rays at Komodo National Park.

categories.name: Budget
categories.summary: Lombok is cheaper — Komodo day trips add $50–100 to Flores costs. Lombok budget: $25–45/day; Flores: $40–80+/day near Labuan Bajo.

categories.name: Diving
categories.summary: Komodo is consistently rated a top-5 dive destination globally. Gili Islands are excellent for beginners.

categories.name: Trekking
categories.summary: Mount Rinjani (3,726m) is one of Southeast Asia's great multi-day volcano treks.

categories.name: Accessibility
categories.summary: 25-minute flight from Bali, easy scooter transport. Flores requires more planning and organized boat tours.

categories.name: Culture
categories.summary: Both unique: Lombok is Sasak Muslim; Flores is predominantly Catholic with animist Ngada highlands culture.

categories.name: Best Time
categories.summary: Both best May–October dry season. Flores July–August can feel crowded at Komodo; shoulder season (May, Sep–Oct) is optimal.

faq.question: Is Lombok or Flores better for first-time visitors to Indonesia?
faq.answer: Lombok is the easier, more accessible starting point for first-timers. Come back for Flores when you're ready for more adventure.

faq.question: Can you do Komodo National Park without staying in Flores?
faq.answer: Yes — fly from Bali directly to Labuan Bajo for 2–3 days focused on Komodo. Budget $150–200 USD for two days including park fees, boat tours, and accommodation.

faq.question: How do you get from Lombok to Flores?
faq.answer: Fly via Bali (4–6 hours with layover), or take the legendary 4-day/3-night sailing boat from Lombok to Labuan Bajo ($200–600 USD depending on boat class).
